prompt: A machine with a persistent data disk is deleted. What happens to the disk?
hint: Is the disk part of the machine?

choices.text: It is erased with the machine, as a drive inside a server would be
choices.why: That is the wrong picture: the disk is a resource on Google's network.

choices.text: It becomes a snapshot automatically
choices.why: No snapshot is taken unless a schedule or a person takes it.

choices.text: It stays, ready to attach to another machine
choices.why: Right. A data disk created on its own outlives the machine.

choices.text: It moves to the regional storage of the project
choices.why: Nothing moves; the disk stays where it was.

prompt: A database on a 50 GiB pd-ssd is slow on disk. Someone proposes a 500 GiB pd-balanced. Why might that be faster?
hint: What does a persistent disk's performance depend on?

choices.text: Performance grows with size, and ten times outweighs the type
choices.why: Right, up to the type's ceiling and the machine's.

choices.text: pd-balanced uses newer SSDs than pd-ssd
choices.why: pd-ssd has more operations per GiB, not fewer.

choices.text: Balanced disks are allowed to skip the machine's own ceiling on operations
choices.why: Every disk gets the lower of its own limit and the machine's.

choices.text: A larger disk is cached in the host's memory
choices.why: Size buys performance per GiB, not a cache.

prompt: Why does the lesson put /dev/disk/by-id/google-orders-data in /etc/fstab rather than /dev/sdb?
hint: Which name stays the same between boots?

choices.text: /dev/sdb is reserved for the boot disk on every Debian machine
choices.why: The boot disk is usually sda; that is not the reason.

choices.text: fstab refuses names that start with /dev/sd
choices.why: It accepts them; they just are not stable.

choices.text: The by-id path is faster to mount
choices.why: Speed is the same; stability differs.

choices.text: /dev/sdb shifts between boots; the by-id name does not
choices.why: Right. The by-id path comes from the name you set in Terraform.

prompt: By the sheet, what does a 200 GiB regional pd-balanced disk cost a month, in USD?
hint: 0.2 per GiB-month.

prompt: A group of stateless web machines keeps nothing on disk that is not in the image. Is a regional disk for each one a good idea?
hint: What would the second copy protect?

choices.text: Yes: a zone failure would otherwise lose the shop's data
choices.why: The data is not on these disks; that is what stateless means.

choices.text: No: the copies exist already, so it pays twice
choices.why: Right. A lost machine is replaced from the image; nothing on its disk is unique.

choices.text: Yes: regional disks are faster to write than zonal ones
choices.why: They are slightly slower, since each write is confirmed twice.

choices.text: No: regional disks cannot be boot disks
choices.why: The objection is the cost of a needless copy, not a rule about boot disks.

prompt: A regional disk writes every block to ___ zones before it confirms the write.
hint: How many copies does it keep?

prompt: A 200 GiB Hyperdisk Balanced is provisioned at 5,000 IOPS and the baseline throughput. At 0.08 per GiB-month and 0.005 per IOPS-month above 3,000, what is a month, in USD?
hint: 16 for the space, plus 2,000 extra IOPS.

prompt: What does Hyperdisk change compared with a persistent disk?
hint: Three things a disk sells.

choices.text: It is attached inside the host, like a local SSD
choices.why: Hyperdisk is network storage, like a persistent disk.

choices.text: It keeps two copies in two zones by default
choices.why: That is a regional disk; Hyperdisk Balanced is zonal unless you choose its HA form.

choices.text: Capacity, IOPS and throughput are bought apart
choices.why: Right. Speed no longer has to come from size.

choices.text: It is billed per operation rather than per GiB
choices.why: Space is still per GiB; the extra performance is per IOPS and per MBps provisioned.

prompt: On an n4-standard-4, the boot disk is changed to pd-balanced and terraform plan succeeds. What happens next?
hint: Which disks does N4 attach?

choices.text: Compute Engine refuses it: N4 uses only Hyperdisk
choices.why: Right. The same limit lessons 1 and 2 met.

choices.text: The machine boots normally, since the plan succeeded
choices.why: A plan checks the file, not the series' rules.

choices.text: Terraform converts the disk to Hyperdisk on apply
choices.why: Nothing converts a type silently.

choices.text: The disk is attached but limited to the baseline 3,000 IOPS
choices.why: It is not attached at all.

prompt: Every Hyperdisk Balanced includes 3,000 IOPS and ___ MBps at no extra charge.
hint: The throughput baseline on the price page.

prompt: A report runs for two days at the end of each month and needs 12,000 IOPS; the rest of the month 3,000 is plenty. What does Hyperdisk allow that a persistent disk does not?
hint: Can a disk shrink?

choices.text: Bursting to 12,000 automatically with no change at all
choices.why: Hyperdisk delivers what is provisioned; it does not burst on its own.

choices.text: Paying for the IOPS only when the report reads the disk
choices.why: Provisioned IOPS are billed while they are set, used or not.

choices.text: Moving the disk to a local SSD for two days
choices.why: A local SSD cannot be attached after creation, and is not where data should live.

choices.text: Raising the IOPS before the report and lowering them after
choices.why: Right. A persistent disk would have to grow, and it cannot shrink back.

prompt: Which of these belongs on a local SSD?
hint: Something that can be rebuilt.

choices.text: The orders database, for speed
choices.why: Its data would be lost with the host.

choices.text: Spill files of a sort
choices.why: Right. Scratch space that a restart can rebuild.

choices.text: The only copy of uploaded photos
choices.why: Never the only copy of anything.

choices.text: The machine's boot disk
choices.why: A machine boots from a persistent disk or Hyperdisk.

prompt: A batch worker with a local SSD is stopped every night to save money. What does it find in the morning?
hint: Stopping moves the machine off its host.

choices.text: Everything as it was, exactly as after an ordinary reboot
choices.why: A reboot keeps the data; a stop does not, unless preserved.

choices.text: The SSD detached and kept as a separate disk
choices.why: A local SSD cannot exist apart from a host.

choices.text: An empty local SSD, unless preservation was requested
choices.why: Right. Stopping is the case that surprises people.

choices.text: A snapshot of the SSD taken at the stop
choices.why: Snapshots are of persistent disks and Hyperdisk, not local SSD.

prompt: At 0.08 per GiB-month, what do four local SSD slices of 375 GiB cost a month, in USD?
hint: One slice is 30.

prompt: Order these events from the one that keeps a local SSD's data to the one that loses it with the machine gone for good.
hint: Reboot and live migration keep it; deletion is final.
items: A live migration to another host
trap: Live migration copies the data to the new host, so it keeps it; a stop does not.

prompt: Why can a local SSD not be added to a running machine the way a persistent disk can?
hint: Where is it?

choices.text: It is part of the host
choices.why: Right. It is attached at creation and never afterwards.

choices.text: Terraform has no resource for local SSDs
choices.why: scratch_disk is how Terraform writes one.

choices.text: Local SSDs are only sold with GPUs
choices.why: An N2 takes them, as this lesson's file shows.

choices.text: It needs a snapshot schedule first
choices.why: Schedules are for persistent disks.

prompt: What does the second snapshot of a disk copy?
hint: Snapshots are incremental.

choices.text: The whole disk again, including empty blocks
choices.why: Even the first copies only what is used.

choices.text: Only the files the application marked for backup
choices.why: A snapshot works on blocks, not files.

choices.text: A copy of the first snapshot plus the changes
choices.why: Nothing is copied twice.

choices.text: Only the blocks that changed since the first
choices.why: Right. That is what makes nightly snapshots cheap.

prompt: The oldest of fourteen snapshots is deleted by the schedule. Is the next one still restorable?
hint: What does Compute Engine do with blocks a newer snapshot still needs?

choices.text: No: it needed the oldest one's blocks, so the chain is broken
choices.why: Deleting never breaks a newer snapshot.

choices.text: Yes: the blocks it needs are moved to it
choices.why: Right. Deletion is safe in any order.

choices.text: Only if it was an archive snapshot
choices.why: The kind does not decide this.

choices.text: Only until the next schedule run
choices.why: It stays restorable for as long as it is kept.

prompt: The schedule says start_time = "04:00". When does it run in São Paulo?
hint: Which clock does the field use?

choices.text: At 04:00, since the policy is in southamerica-east1
choices.why: The region does not set the time zone of the field.

choices.text: At 04:00 in Iowa, where the prices come from
choices.why: The price sheet has nothing to do with schedules.

choices.text: At 01:00, because the field is in UTC
choices.why: Right. São Paulo is three hours behind UTC.

choices.text: At a random time within four hours
choices.why: The time is the one written, in UTC.

prompt: A disk has 60 GiB in use and about 2 GiB changing a day. Ten nightly snapshots are kept. At most how many GiB do they hold, before compression?
hint: The first holds what is used; each of the other nine holds a day of changes.

prompt: Why does the lesson set on_source_disk_delete = "KEEP_AUTO_SNAPSHOTS"?
hint: When are snapshots needed most?

choices.text: So that deleting the wrong disk leaves its snapshots to restore from
choices.why: Right. That day is when the snapshots matter.

choices.text: It makes the snapshots cheaper to store
choices.why: It changes what survives, not the price.

choices.text: Without it, the plan fails
choices.why: The field is optional; a misspelt value fails, not a missing one.

choices.text: It keeps the disk from being deleted at all
choices.why: The disk can still be deleted; the snapshots stay.

prompt: A snapshot of a disk in use is crash-___: what you would find after pulling the power.
hint: Not application-consistent.

prompt: Match each need to the storage this lesson recommends.
hint: Durability, two zones, speed bought separately, scratch.

pairs.left: A data disk that outlives its machine
A database with no replica that must survive a zone failure
A database on N4 needing 6,000 IOPS on 100 GiB
The spill files of a big sort

prompt: The orders-data disk is deleted by mistake on a Tuesday. With the lesson's schedule in place, what is the restore?
hint: A restore never writes over anything.

choices.text: Undelete the disk from the recycle bin of the zone
choices.why: The lesson's answer is the snapshots it kept.

choices.text: Restore the disk in place from the archive snapshot
choices.why: The schedule keeps standard snapshots, and a restore makes a new disk.

choices.text: Nothing: the snapshots went with the disk
choices.why: KEEP_AUTO_SNAPSHOTS is there to prevent exactly that.

choices.text: Make a new disk from Monday night's snapshot
choices.why: Right. The snapshots stayed, and the newest one has the data to 04:00 UTC.

prompt: By the sheet, how much more a month does a 100 GiB pd-ssd cost than a 100 GiB pd-balanced, in USD?
hint: 0.17 against 0.1 per GiB-month.
